tasks.spec: You are a code worker adding a raw-language regression corpus to the freytag-forge text-adventure engine. Edit files ONLY under the current working directory; NEVER edit anything under /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge directly (you may only run its .venv/bin/python). Do NOT git commit. Workers cannot run uv: run Python as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python ...`. Do not change any runtime code under storygame/ and do not edit any file you do not own. You own exactly two new files: tests/fixtures/raw_language_corpus.json and tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py. BACKGROUND: the story at data/stories/continuity-initiative has authored reveals (knowledge records with `action_evidence`). `storygame.runtime.candidate_matcher.uniquely_matched_authored_handoff(player_input, candidates)` decides deterministically whether typed input earns one reveal; see tests/test_copied_files_pilot.py (function test_2c_copied_file_commands_match_only_the_original_reveal) for how to build the candidates for a scene: `tuple(item for item in PACKAGE.knowledge.knowledge if '<SCENE>' in item.available_in_scenes and item.action_evidence)` with `PACKAGE = load_story_package(Path('data/stories/continuity-initiative'))`. The repo's normal test inputs are terse imperatives. This corpus deliberately uses the way real players type: it measures the matcher, it does NOT widen it. TASK: for each of the scenes 1A, 2A and 2C, pick two reveals that have `action_evidence` (read data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml). For each reveal write one `canonical` command that the matcher currently accepts (run the matcher to confirm), then PAIRED variants of that same command in the same scene, covering these kinds (use each kind at least once per scene, 8 or more variants per scene): `polite` (Please check my copied JANUS files.), `pronoun` (Check them. is NOT enough alone: use a form that still names the object only by pronoun after a first clause, e.g. Pick up the drive and check it.), `correction` (Actually, open the files instead.), `scene_listening` (a listen-style command where something in that scene could be heard, e.g. Listen to the recording. only if a reveal mentions it; otherwise skip this kind for that scene), `unrelated_restraint` (the act plus an unrelated restraint clause, e.g. Check my copied JANUS files, but do not send anything yet.), `first_person` (I check my copied JANUS files.), and `clarification_needed` (input so vague that a human would ask what is meant, e.g. Do the thing with it.). Also add 2 `near_miss` entries per scene that look similar but are NOT the act (the correct outcome is no reveal). FILE FORMAT: tests/fixtures/raw_language_corpus.json is a list of objects {id, scene, reveal_id, kind, input, intended, observed, note}. `intended` is what a reasonable player means: the reveal id, or null (no reveal / needs clarification). `observed` is what the real matcher returns TODAY (the reveal id or null), found by RUNNING it, never guessed. `note` is one short sentence. TESTS (tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py, no network, no model): (1) every entry's `observed` equals what the matcher returns now (parametrised, ids from entry id); (2) every canonical entry is observed == intended == its reveal_id; (3) every near_miss and clarification_needed entry has intended null; (4) any entry whose intended != observed is a known gap and its note must start with `GAP:` (so a future matcher change forces an update of the file); (5) a summary test asserts the file has at least 24 entries, every listed kind appears, and prints (via a captured assertion message only on failure) nothing else. Do not edit the matcher to make entries pass; the point is to record gaps honestly. Write a short notes file at /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/design-review-step9-notes/corpus.md (create the directory) listing the count of entries per kind and the number of GAP entries per kind. FINISH by running: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py and then /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff format tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py.

tasks.spec: You are a code worker adding a raw-language player profile to the freytag-forge blind-player test harness. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files ONLY under the current working directory; NEVER edit anything under /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge directly (you may only run its .venv/bin/python). Do NOT git commit. Workers cannot run uv: run Python as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python ...`. Do not change anything under storygame/ and do not edit any file you do not own. You own exactly: frontend/e2e/blind-player.js, frontend/e2e/blind-player.test.js and frontend/e2e/blind-player.spec.js. BACKGROUND: frontend/e2e/blind-player.js asks an LLM to play the game. Today it has one style, `canonical`: PLAYER_SYSTEM demands imperative, first-person-possessive, active commands, and validateCommand(command) rejects commands starting with I, restraint words, commands starting with wait/listen/keep watch/stand still/continue waiting, commands without a final period, and anything outside 2 to 25 words. That style stays the default and its behaviour must not change. TASK: add a second profile `raw` that models how real people type. (1) Export PROFILES or a profile lookup. Select it with the environment variable BLIND_PLAYER_PROFILE (values canonical | raw; unset or unknown value = canonical; unknown values must be reported in the bundle/turn record rather than silently accepted). (2) `raw` has its own system prompt: write one natural command as a person would type it; polite requests, pronouns, corrections of an earlier command, and listening when there is something to hear are all allowed; no JSON, no explanation. Write it in plain words, 12th-grade reading level, short sentences. (3) validateCommand(command, profile = 'canonical'): for `raw` do NOT reject I-forms, restraint words, listen/wait starts or a missing final period; only require non-empty text of 1 to 40 words and no newline. Canonical rules are unchanged. (4) askPlayer takes an optional `profile` (default read from the environment) and validates with that profile. (5) turnRecord gets two new fields: `raw_input` (the exact text the player model returned, untouched) and `profile` (the profile name); the existing `input` stays as it is today (the text sent to the game). In `raw` the game receives the raw text unchanged. (6) analyseRun/aggregate output carry the `profile` so a report shows which profile produced a run; if a run mixes profiles, say so. (7) blind-player.spec.js passes the profile through to askPlayer and turnRecord. TESTS in frontend/e2e/blind-player.test.js (node --test, no network): canonical validation unchanged (existing tests still pass); raw accepts `Please open my laptop`, `I check the drive`, `Listen to the recording` and `Open it, but don't send anything yet`; raw rejects an empty string, a 45-word string and a string with a newline; unknown profile name falls back to canonical and is flagged; turnRecord keeps raw_input and profile; the raw system prompt does not contain the word `imperative`. FINISH by running from the worktree: cd frontend && node --test e2e/blind-player.test.js (node_modules are not needed for this file). Write a short notes file at /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/design-review-step9-notes/profile.md (create the directory) saying what changed.
